English: Community Room
A humble, makeshift gathering space of tents and benches where townsfolk meet for basic discussion and resolve disputes.
Meeting Hall
A sturdier timber structure with a raised platform, allowing more formal assemblies and the beginnings of organized record-keeping.
Rabbinic Chamber
A discreet council room with reinforced doors and scroll racks, where trusted advisors gather to strategize and resolve local disputes.
Judicial Chamber
A high-walled stone room with benches for adjudicators, where justice is dispensed and records are kept under lock and key.
Council Chamber
A well-built chamber within the keep, decorated with banners and benches, dedicated to the meetings of elders and councilors.
Stone Assembly Room
A fortified stone hall with carved seating and secure doors, providing a safe place for critical deliberations and plans.
Elders' Hall
A grand hall adorned with carved pillars and stonework, where the leading elders and council meet to govern and command.
Community Assembly
An ornate hall with elaborate woodwork, a dais for the lord or mayor, and antechambers for private counsel, fostering unity and order.
Great Hall
A vast stone hall with vaulted ceilings, banners, and ceremonial tables, serving as the heart of governance and feudal ceremony.
Grand Council Hall
A resplendent hall of marble and gold, with galleries for advisors and scribes, serving as the seat of the highest council and command.
